claimed_purpose.text: Intelligent memory ingestion with Prediction Error Gating — automatically decides whether to create, update, or supersede memories based on semantic similarity to existing content.
Records retrieval telemetry without reinforcing memories; positive feedback through memory(action='promote') is the explicit strengthening signal.
Preview mode does not mutate the graph; explicit promotion persists edges and reinforces nodes.
Queryless memory layer for multi-agent coding fleets
Local-first design with FSRS-based memory scheduling

mechanisms.text: Source-aware filters allow post-filtering retrieved memories by external system, project, id, type, author, update time, and validity status (valid/tombstoned); tombstoned records are kept in the store for audit even after removal upstream.

Retrieval is audit-only; a recalled memory being shown does not strengthen it. An explicit promote signal is required to strengthen a memory after it proves useful, preventing stale results from becoming self-reinforcing.

purge is an irreversible delete operation, being split into its own advertised MCP tool with requiresUserInteraction and destructiveHint: true; memory(action='purge') is kept as an alias for one release.
Memory state is derived from retention_strength: Active (>0.7), Dormant (>0.4), Silent (>0.1), Unavailable (<=0.1), and each state produces an accessibility multiplier on the combined score.
On ingest, Vestige compares new content against existing memories by similarity score and either reinforces, updates, or creates a new memory entry — the write path has three branches.
Explicit purge (hard delete): memory(action="purge", confirm=true) permanently removes content and embeddings, scrubs internal references, and keeps only a non-content tombstone.
Risk-gated review of destructive (memory-mutating) writes is implemented via gate_writes and gate_pending_memory_mutation, intended to fire before destructive writes execute.
Vector search uses an embedding profile system that enforces a declared dimension; mismatched dimensions abort storage initialisation and block all memory retrieval.
Outcome labeling provides a write-path feedback loop: users can tag composition results as helpful, dead end, accepted, rejected, duplicate risk, or needs proof.
The MCP check path evaluates triggers with its own logic, handling only 'time' and 'context' trigger types; recurring intentions fall through to a false branch.
Storage engine: SQLite with optional SQLCipher encryption; retrieval uses Nomic Embed v1.5 embeddings + USearch HNSW + SQLite FTS5 with optional Qwen3 reranker
The purge tool is gated behind confirm=true inside a tool that is mostly reads, making it difficult for the host to treat it differently from other actions.
Stats distinguish never-accessed memories from access-unknown-pruned-log memories; agents must not suppress or purge pre-prune memories on access grounds
Isolation: per data directory, supporting shared (multi-agent pointing to same --data-dir) or separate (each agent its own directory) configurations.
A dedup reflog tracks supersede operations and supports undo; this is the documented reversible merge path, but consolidation-cycle merges bypass it.
Suppress is distinct from delete: the memory row persists in storage but is inhibited from retrieval and decays faster via FSRS state degradation.
Write path uses smart_ingest to persist durable preferences, project decisions, recurring corrections, stable facts, and reusable code patterns.
Retrieval score (retrievability) is computed from stability and elapsed days before each review and returned alongside updated state
Isolation is per scope (project namespace). Recall searches within the scope unless includeCrossScope=true. Default scope is 'user'.
Store isolation is per-scope; ordinary operations default to user scope; cross-scope maintenance requires explicit all_scopes=true
Durable audit log for tag operations committed in the same transaction as the mutation; audit reason is screened for credentials
Referenced open issue #85 describes a Trust Zones / Memory Quarantine direction, implying a quarantine state for stored memories
The schema includes bitemporal validity columns (valid_from / valid_until) on knowledge_nodes, though currently unpopulated
Vestige tracks provenance from generated rule lines back to memory IDs, linking output to the originating memory record.
Receipt mechanism: every retrieval and consequential write produces a signed receipt naming the exact evidence path
Hybrid search combines keyword and semantic scoring with RRF fusion, using a 0.3/0.7 keyword/semantic weight split.
A scope column exists in the schema, intended for project-level namespace partitioning at ingest and recall
Memories are never deleted automatically — they fade in accessibility but are not removed from the store.
The in-memory prospective memory engine is never hydrated from storage; it is always empty in production.
Write path — novelty-gated ingestion: only novel facts are stored; redundant writes are merged on write.
Memories are scoped to a namespace; cross-scope inference is not performed. Scope defaults to 'user'.
Intentions are persisted to SQLite storage via the MCP path, not held in the in-memory engine.
Write path tool: smart_ingest gates writes for novelty and contradiction before persisting
Sensitive memory writes can require promotion or approval before becoming durable policy
Forget / suppress mechanism: Active Forgetting provides reversible top-down suppression
Managed Continuity backup and restore — encrypted archive portable across machines.
Search, ingest, lifecycle, purge, suppress, and protect are free local primitives
Vestige surfaces contradictions between memories rather than flattening them.
Data isolation: local only, no cloud, no telemetry
